sents.t: Hello everyone! Welcome to Open Talk! My name is Ethan.
sents.zh: 大家好！欢迎收听 Open Talk！我是 Ethan。

sents.t: And I'm Paula.
sents.zh: 我是 Paula。

sents.t: And this is our very first episode, and we are so happy you're here.
sents.zh: 这是我们的第一期节目，很高兴你来收听。

sents.t: Yes! Today we have a really useful lesson for you.
sents.zh: 是的！今天我们给大家准备了一节特别实用的课。

sents.t: That's right. Today with Paula we're going to talk about wanting things — maybe too many things.
sents.zh: 没错。今天我和 Paula 要聊聊“想要东西”这件事——也许是想要的太多了。

sents.t: Ugh, I know that feeling. A new phone, a bigger apartment, a better job...
sents.zh: 唉，我太懂那种感觉了。新手机、更大的公寓、更好的工作……

sents.t: Right. And then you feel like you can't be happy until you get all of it.
sents.zh: 对。然后你就会觉得，不把这些全部拿到手，自己就快乐不起来。

sents.t: Exactly. In today's lesson, two friends talk about this problem, and you'll learn some great language for talking about what you want — and what you don't.
sents.zh: 正是这样。在今天的课里，两个朋友会聊到这个问题，你会学到一些很棒的表达，用来说说你想要什么——以及你不想要什么。

sents.t: The idea comes from a thinker named Naval Ravikant. He has a simple but powerful way of looking at desire.
sents.zh: 这个想法来自一位叫 Naval Ravikant 的思想家。他看待欲望的方式简单，但很有力量。

sents.t: Don't worry if that sounds a little serious. The dialogue is a normal conversation, the kind you might have after work.
sents.zh: 如果听起来有点严肃，别担心。对话就是一段普通的聊天，就像你下班后会和朋友聊的那种。

sents.t: Great. So, Paula, why don't we start with our "vocabulary preview"?
sents.zh: 好的。那 Paula，我们先从“词汇预习”开始吧？

sents.t: We have two words in our vocabulary preview today. The first is desire.
sents.zh: 今天的词汇预习有两个词。第一个是 desire。

sents.t: Desire.
sents.zh: Desire（欲望）。

sents.t: Desire.
sents.zh: Desire（欲望）。

sents.t: Desire.
sents.zh: Desire（欲望）。

sents.t: So, a desire is a strong feeling that you want to have something, or do something.
sents.zh: Desire 就是一种强烈的感觉，你很想拥有某样东西，或很想做某件事。

sents.t: Right. It's stronger than just "I kind of want it." It's "I really want it."
sents.zh: 对。它比“我有点想要”更强烈，是“我真的很想要”。

sents.t: For example, she has a strong desire to open her own studio.
sents.zh: 比如：她非常渴望开一间属于自己的工作室。

sents.t: Okay. Our second word today is contract.
sents.zh: 好的。今天的第二个词是 contract。

sents.t: Contract.
sents.zh: Contract（契约；合同）。

sents.t: Contract.
sents.zh: Contract（契约；合同）。

sents.t: Contract.
sents.zh: Contract（契约；合同）。

sents.t: A contract is an agreement between two sides. You say yes, I say yes, and now we both have to follow it.
sents.zh: Contract 就是双方之间的约定。你答应，我也答应，然后我们都得遵守。

sents.t: Like when you sign a contract with a salon, or with an apartment.
sents.zh: 就像你和美睫店签合同，或者租房时签的合同。

sents.t: Exactly. Now, in today's dialogue, you'll hear these two words together: desire contract.
sents.zh: 没错。在今天的对话里，你会听到这两个词放在一起：desire contract。

sents.t: Desire contract.
sents.zh: Desire contract（欲望契约）。

sents.t: Desire contract.
sents.zh: Desire contract（欲望契约）。

sents.t: This is a special idea. A desire contract is a contract you make with yourself. You are saying, "I will be unhappy until I get what I want."
sents.zh: 这是一个很特别的概念。“欲望契约”是你和自己签的一份契约。你在对自己说：“得不到我想要的，我就不快乐。”

sents.t: So every new desire is one more contract you sign — with you.
sents.zh: 所以每多一个新的欲望，就是你又和自己签了一份契约。

sents.t: These two words come straight from our dialogue. So, why don't we just listen?
sents.zh: 这两个词都直接来自我们的对话。那我们就来听听吧？

sents.t: Ugh, I spent all night looking at new phones. I want the latest one so badly.
sents.zh: 唉，我昨晚一整晚都在看新手机。我太想要最新款了。

sents.t: Didn't you just get a new phone last year?
sents.zh: 你不是去年才换了新手机吗？

sents.t: Yeah, but this one is better. And I also want to rent a bigger studio. And maybe start selling my own lash products.
sents.zh: 是啊，可这款更好。而且我还想租一间更大的工作室。说不定还要开始卖我自己的睫毛产品。

sents.t: Lily, that's a lot of wants at the same time.
sents.zh: Lily，你同时想要的东西也太多了吧。

sents.t: I know. I just feel like I can't be happy until I get all of it.
sents.zh: 我知道。我就是觉得，不把这些全部拿到手，我就快乐不起来。

sents.t: I heard an interesting idea about that. People say a desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want. Every new desire is one more desire contract you sign.
sents.zh: 关于这个，我听过一个挺有意思的说法。有人说，欲望就是你和自己签的一份契约：得不到想要的，就让自己不快乐。每多一个新的欲望，就是又签了一份欲望契约。

sents.t: A contract with myself? So I'm making myself unhappy on purpose?
sents.zh: 和我自己签的契约？所以我是故意让自己不快乐？

sents.t: Not on purpose. But we pick up a lot of unnecessary desires everywhere — ads, videos, other people's lives.
sents.zh: 不是故意的。但我们会从各种地方沾染上很多没必要的欲望——广告、视频、别人的生活。

sents.t: That's true. I pick them up without even thinking.
sents.zh: 确实。我连想都没想就沾上了。

sents.t: If you want to be really good at your work, you have to be choosy about your desires. You have to focus.
sents.zh: 如果你想把工作做得真正出色，就得对自己的欲望有所挑选。你得专注。

sents.t: Frankly, I can't be great at everything. I'll just waste my energy.
sents.zh: 说实话，我不可能样样都做得很好。那样我只会浪费精力。

sents.t: Exactly. Maybe keep one desire, and let the others go for now.
sents.zh: 没错。也许先留下一个欲望，其他的暂时放一放。

sents.t: Okay. The studio can wait. The phone can wait. I'll focus on my clients this year.
sents.zh: 好吧。工作室可以等等，手机也可以等等。今年我就专心照顾好我的客人。

sents.t: Wow, Paula, Lily wants a lot of things at the same time.
sents.zh: 哇，Paula，Lily 同时想要的东西真多。

sents.t: I think a lot of us do.
sents.zh: 我觉得我们很多人都是这样。

sents.t: Yeah. And that idea — a desire contract — is really interesting. We'll talk more about that later. But first, let's hear how Naval himself said it.
sents.zh: 是啊。而“欲望契约”这个想法真的很有意思。我们待会儿再细聊。不过先来听听 Naval 本人是怎么说的。

sents.t: This is from the original interview. First you'll hear a question from Chris, then Naval's own words.
sents.zh: 这段来自原始访谈。你会先听到 Chris 的提问，然后是 Naval 的原话。

sents.t: How do you shortcut that desire contract?
sents.zh: 怎样才能绕过这种“欲望契约”——也就是“得不到就不允许自己快乐”的约定？

sents.t: You could focus, you could decide that I don’t want most things.
sents.zh: 你可以专注，你可以决定：大多数东西我都不想要。

sents.t: I think we have a lot of unnecessary desires that we just pick up everywhere, have opinions on everything, judgments on everything,
sents.zh: 我觉得，我们有很多其实没必要的欲望，是在生活中不知不觉沾染来的；我们对什么都想发表意见，对什么都想评头论足。

sents.t: so I think just knowing that those are the source of unhappiness will make you be choosy about your desires.
sents.zh: 只要意识到这些欲望正是不幸福的来源，你就会更谨慎地选择自己究竟要追求什么。

sents.t: And frankly if you want to be successful, you have to be choosy about your desires, you have to focus.
sents.zh: 而且说真的，如果你想有所成就，就必须有所取舍，认真选择自己的欲望，把精力集中在重要的事情上。

sents.t: You can’t be great at everything. You’re just going to waste your energy and waste your time.
sents.zh: 你不可能样样都做得很好。那样你只会浪费精力，浪费时间。

sents.t: That's Naval in his own voice. Now it's time for "language takeaway".
sents.zh: 这就是 Naval 本人的声音。现在进入“语言要点”环节。

sents.t: There's some great language in this dialogue. Let's start with our first word: shortcut.
sents.zh: 这段对话里有很多好用的表达。我们先从第一个词开始：shortcut。

sents.t: Shortcut.
sents.zh: Shortcut（走捷径；绕过）。

sents.t: Shortcut.
sents.zh: Shortcut（走捷径；绕过）。

sents.t: Shortcut.
sents.zh: Shortcut（走捷径；绕过）。

sents.t: To shortcut something means to find a quicker way to do it — you skip the long way.
sents.zh: Shortcut 一件事，就是找到更快的办法去做——跳过那条远路。

sents.t: In the original idea, someone asks: how do you shortcut that desire contract? Is there a quicker way out of it?
sents.zh: 在原来的说法里，有人问：怎样才能绕过那份欲望契约？有没有更快的出路？

sents.t: Right. You don't have to keep every contract you signed with yourself.
sents.zh: 对。你不必遵守你和自己签过的每一份契约。

sents.t: Let's go to our next phrase now: pick up.
sents.zh: 现在来看下一个短语：pick up。

sents.t: Pick up.
sents.zh: Pick up（这里指：不知不觉沾上）。

sents.t: Pick up.
sents.zh: Pick up（这里指：不知不觉沾上）。

sents.t: Pick up.
sents.zh: Pick up（这里指：不知不觉沾上）。

sents.t: Now, "pick up" can mean "lift something from the floor," but in this dialogue it has a different meaning.
sents.zh: “Pick up”可以指“把东西从地上捡起来”，但在这段对话里，它是另一个意思。

sents.t: Here, to pick up a desire means to start having it, often without planning to. You just get it from the world around you.
sents.zh: 在这里，pick up 一个欲望，是指开始有了它，而且往往不是你计划好的。你只是从周围的世界里沾染上了它。

sents.t: We have some examples. Let's listen.
sents.zh: 我们准备了一些例子，一起听听吧。

sents.t: Example one.
sents.zh: 例一。

sents.t: Kids pick up bad words at school.
sents.zh: 孩子们在学校学会了说脏话。

sents.t: Example two.
sents.zh: 例二。

sents.t: I picked up a few new skills from YouTube.
sents.zh: 我从 YouTube 上学会了几项新技能。

sents.t: Example three.
sents.zh: 例三。

sents.t: Be careful. It's easy to pick up other people's stress.
sents.zh: 小心点。别人的压力很容易传染给你。

sents.t: So you can pick up a habit, an idea, or a desire.
sents.zh: 所以你可以 pick up 一个习惯、一个想法，或者一个欲望。

sents.t: Exactly. Our next word is choosy.
sents.zh: 没错。下一个词是 choosy。

sents.t: Choosy.
sents.zh: Choosy（挑剔的；有选择的）。

sents.t: Choosy.
sents.zh: Choosy（挑剔的；有选择的）。

sents.t: Choosy.
sents.zh: Choosy（挑剔的；有选择的）。

sents.t: If you are choosy, you are careful about what you accept. You don't want just anything.
sents.zh: 如果你很 choosy，就是你对接受什么很挑剔、很谨慎，不是随便什么都要。

sents.t: For example: she's very choosy about her lash glue. She doesn't use just any glue.
sents.zh: 比如：她对睫毛胶水很挑，不是随便哪种胶水都用。

sents.t: And in the dialogue: you have to be choosy about your desires. Don't say yes to every want.
sents.zh: 在对话里是：你得对自己的欲望有所挑选。别对每个“想要”都说好。

sents.t: Okay, our next word is frankly.
sents.zh: 好的，下一个词是 frankly。

sents.t: Frankly.
sents.zh: Frankly（坦白说）。

sents.t: Frankly.
sents.zh: Frankly（坦白说）。

sents.t: Frankly.
sents.zh: Frankly（坦白说）。

sents.t: We use frankly when we say what we really think, in a direct way.
sents.zh: 当我们直截了当地说出真实想法时，就会用 frankly。

sents.t: Frankly, I don't like this style.
sents.zh: 说实话，我不喜欢这种风格。

sents.t: Frankly, I can't be great at everything.
sents.zh: 说实话，我不可能样样都做得很好。

sents.t: It's like saying, "I'm going to be honest with you."
sents.zh: 这就像在说：“我跟你说实话吧。”

sents.t: And our last phrase today is the source of unhappiness.
sents.zh: 今天最后一个短语是 the source of unhappiness。

sents.t: The source of unhappiness.
sents.zh: The source of unhappiness（不快乐的来源）。

sents.t: The source of unhappiness.
sents.zh: The source of unhappiness（不快乐的来源）。

sents.t: A source is the place something comes from. Unhappiness is the feeling of not being happy.
sents.zh: Source 是某样东西的来源。Unhappiness 是不快乐的感觉。

sents.t: So in this idea, too many desires are the source of unhappiness. You feel unhappy because you keep signing new contracts with yourself.
sents.zh: 所以按照这个观点，欲望太多就是不快乐的来源。你之所以不快乐，是因为你不停地和自己签新的契约。

sents.t: I think that's pretty clear.
sents.zh: 我觉得这挺清楚的。

sents.t: Yeah. Now, Paula, let's look at how some of these phrases work together.
sents.zh: 是啊。那 Paula，我们来看看这些短语怎么搭配在一起用。

sents.t: In this section, "putting it together," we show you how to combine useful phrases, so you can say a complete idea, not just single words.
sents.zh: 在“组合运用”这个环节，我们会教你怎么把实用的短语组合起来，让你能说出完整的意思，而不只是单个的词。

sents.t: Right. In the dialogue, Mark says: you have to be choosy about your desires. You have to focus.
sents.zh: 对。在对话里，Mark 说：你得对自己的欲望有所挑选，你得专注。

sents.t: And Lily answers: frankly, I can't be great at everything. I'll just waste my energy.
sents.zh: Lily 回答：说实话，我不可能样样都做得很好，那样我只会浪费精力。

sents.t: So let's put that together. If you want to be good at your work, you cannot want everything.
sents.zh: 我们把它连起来说：如果你想把工作做好，就不能什么都想要。

sents.t: Let's listen to a few ways to say this.
sents.zh: 我们来听几种说法。

sents.t: Example one.
sents.zh: 例一。

sents.t: If you want to do great work, you have to be choosy about your desires. You have to focus.
sents.zh: 如果你想做出很棒的成绩，就得对自己的欲望有所挑选。你得专注。

sents.t: Example two.
sents.zh: 例二。

sents.t: Frankly, you can't be great at everything. You'll just waste your energy and waste your time.
sents.zh: 说实话，你不可能样样都做得很好。那样你只会浪费精力，浪费时间。

sents.t: Example three.
sents.zh: 例三。

sents.t: I need to be choosy. I can't focus if I want too many things at the same time.
sents.zh: 我得有所取舍。同时想要太多东西，我就没法专注。

sents.t: So you can start with "you have to be choosy about..." and then add "you have to focus."
sents.zh: 所以你可以先说“you have to be choosy about...”，再接一句“you have to focus”。

sents.t: Or you can be direct: "Frankly, I can't be great at everything. So I'll focus on this one thing for now."
sents.zh: 或者你也可以直接说：“说实话，我不可能样样都做得很好。所以眼下我先专注这一件事。”

sents.t: That's a really useful sentence in real life. Okay, Paula, now let's look at how to say some of these phrases more naturally.
sents.zh: 这在现实生活里是很实用的一句话。好，Paula，现在我们来看看怎么把这些短语说得更地道。

sents.t: In "fluency builder," we look at phrases that help you sound more natural — the way people really talk.
sents.zh: 在“流利表达”环节，我们会学一些让你听起来更自然的短语——就是大家真正说话的方式。

sents.t: That's right. Let's listen to the first one from the dialogue.
sents.zh: 没错。我们来听对话里的第一个。

sents.t: Phrase one: I can't be happy until I get all of it. I can't be happy until I get all of it.
sents.zh: 短语一：不把这些全部拿到手，我就快乐不起来。不把这些全部拿到手，我就快乐不起来。

sents.t: This is the desire contract in everyday words. "I can't be happy until..."
sents.zh: 这就是用日常的话说出来的欲望契约：“我没法快乐，除非……”

sents.t: You can change the ending: I can't be happy until I finish this. I can't be happy until I move to a new place.
sents.zh: 你可以换掉后半句：做完这件事之前，我快乐不起来。搬到新地方之前，我快乐不起来。

sents.t: But remember: that sentence is a contract. You're telling yourself to wait before you feel okay.
sents.zh: 但要记住：这句话本身就是一份契约。你在告诉自己，要等到那之后才能觉得还不错。

sents.t: Yeah. Next phrase.
sents.zh: 是啊。下一个短语。

sents.t: Phrase two: I pick them up without even thinking. I pick them up without even thinking.
sents.zh: 短语二：我连想都没想就沾上了。我连想都没想就沾上了。

sents.t: "Without even thinking" means it happens automatically. You don't plan it.
sents.zh: “Without even thinking”的意思是事情自动就发生了，你并没有计划。

sents.t: I say yes without even thinking. I buy things without even thinking.
sents.zh: 我连想都没想就答应了。我连想都没想就买了东西。

sents.t: Very natural, and very common.
sents.zh: 非常自然，也非常常用。

sents.t: And our last phrase today is a soft way to let something go.
sents.zh: 今天最后一个短语，是一种温和地放下某件事的说法。

sents.t: Phrase three: Let the others go for now. Let the others go for now.
sents.zh: 短语三：其他的暂时放一放。其他的暂时放一放。

sents.t: "For now" is a really friendly little chunk. It means "not forever, just at this time."
sents.zh: “For now”是个很友好的小语块，意思是“不是永远，只是眼下”。

sents.t: The studio can wait for now. I'll focus on my clients for now.
sents.zh: 工作室暂时可以先等等。眼下我先专心照顾我的客人。

sents.t: You don't have to say no forever. You just say, not right now.
sents.zh: 你不必永远说不。你只是说：现在先不。

sents.t: Okay, great. I think we're ready to listen to our dialogue a second time. This time, try to catch these phrases.
sents.zh: 好，太棒了。我想我们可以再听一遍对话了。这次试着听出这些短语。

sents.t: Ugh, I spent all night looking at new phones. I want the latest one so badly.
sents.zh: 唉，我昨晚一整晚都在看新手机。我太想要最新款了。

sents.t: Didn't you just get a new phone last year?
sents.zh: 你不是去年才换了新手机吗？

sents.t: Yeah, but this one is better. And I also want to rent a bigger studio. And maybe start selling my own lash products.
sents.zh: 是啊，可这款更好。而且我还想租一间更大的工作室。说不定还要开始卖我自己的睫毛产品。

sents.t: Lily, that's a lot of wants at the same time.
sents.zh: Lily，你同时想要的东西也太多了吧。

sents.t: I know. I just feel like I can't be happy until I get all of it.
sents.zh: 我知道。我就是觉得，不把这些全部拿到手，我就快乐不起来。

sents.t: I heard an interesting idea about that. People say a desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want. Every new desire is one more desire contract you sign.
sents.zh: 关于这个，我听过一个挺有意思的说法。有人说，欲望就是你和自己签的一份契约：得不到想要的，就让自己不快乐。每多一个新的欲望，就是又签了一份欲望契约。

sents.t: A contract with myself? So I'm making myself unhappy on purpose?
sents.zh: 和我自己签的契约？所以我是故意让自己不快乐？

sents.t: Not on purpose. But we pick up a lot of unnecessary desires everywhere — ads, videos, other people's lives.
sents.zh: 不是故意的。但我们会从各种地方沾染上很多没必要的欲望——广告、视频、别人的生活。

sents.t: That's true. I pick them up without even thinking.
sents.zh: 确实。我连想都没想就沾上了。

sents.t: If you want to be really good at your work, you have to be choosy about your desires. You have to focus.
sents.zh: 如果你想把工作做得真正出色，就得对自己的欲望有所挑选。你得专注。

sents.t: Frankly, I can't be great at everything. I'll just waste my energy.
sents.zh: 说实话，我不可能样样都做得很好。那样我只会浪费精力。

sents.t: Exactly. Maybe keep one desire, and let the others go for now.
sents.zh: 没错。也许先留下一个欲望，其他的暂时放一放。

sents.t: Okay. The studio can wait. The phone can wait. I'll focus on my clients this year.
sents.zh: 好吧。工作室可以等等，手机也可以等等。今年我就专心照顾好我的客人。

sents.t: Okay, Paula, so what do you think about this idea — the desire contract?
sents.zh: 好，Paula，你怎么看这个想法——欲望契约？

sents.t: I think it's a little uncomfortable, Ethan, but it's true.
sents.zh: Ethan，我觉得它让人有点不舒服，但说的是真的。

sents.t: Uncomfortable?
sents.zh: 不舒服？

sents.t: Yeah, because I do this all the time. I see a nice bag, or a new course, or a better apartment, and suddenly I feel like my life is not enough.
sents.zh: 是啊，因为我总是这样。看到一个好看的包，或者一门新课程，或者一间更好的公寓，突然就觉得自己的生活不够好了。

sents.t: Right. You pick up a new desire, and then you sign that contract: I will be unhappy until I get it.
sents.zh: 对。你沾上了一个新的欲望，然后就签下那份契约：得不到它，我就不快乐。

sents.t: Exactly. And frankly, I can't go after everything. I'll just waste my energy.
sents.zh: 正是。而且说实话，我不可能什么都去追。那样我只会浪费精力。

sents.t: Same here. I think the useful part is to be choosy. Keep one or two desires that really matter, and let the others go for now.
sents.zh: 我也是。我觉得有用的地方就在于要有所挑选。留下一两个真正重要的欲望，其他的暂时放一放。

sents.t: Yes. Focus. You can't be great at everything.
sents.zh: 对。专注。你不可能样样都做得很好。

sents.t: That's a good sentence to take with you this week.
sents.zh: 这句话很适合你这一周带在身边。

sents.t: Listeners, after this episode, maybe ask yourself: which desire contracts have I signed? And which ones can wait?
sents.zh: 各位听众，听完这期节目，也许可以问问自己：我签下了哪些欲望契约？哪些可以先等一等？

sents.t: You don't have to answer us. Just think about it the next time you want something new.
sents.zh: 不用回答我们。下次你又想要新东西的时候，想一想就好。

sents.t: And that's all for our first episode of Open Talk. Thanks for listening.
sents.zh: 我们 Open Talk 的第一期节目就到这里。谢谢收听。

sents.t: We'll be back soon with another everyday conversation, and more useful English.
sents.zh: 我们很快会带着另一段日常对话和更多实用英语回来。

sents.t: Until next time... goodbye!
sents.zh: 下次见……再见！

sents.t: Bye!
sents.zh: 拜拜！
